basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Evigilans autem Noe ex vino, cum didicisset quae fecerat ei filius suus minor, ait:'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Evigilans autem Noe ex vino, cum didicisset quae fecerat ei filius suus minor, ait: Maledictus Chanaam, servus servorum erit fratribus suis. Evigilans ex vino Noe progeniem ejus a qua irrisus est maledicit; eos vero qui se ut patrem honoravere benedictione debita remunerat; et Dominus juxta vocem psalmi (Psal. III, 6) cum dormisset in morte, ac resurgeret immortalis, percussit omnes adversantes sibi sine causa, dentesque peccatorum contrivit; super populum vero suum benedictionem perpetuae salutis profudit. Non solum autem Chanaam maledictioni, sed etiam servitio fratrum suorum subjicitur. Quid est enim aliud hodie gens ipsa, nisi quaedam scriniaria Christianorum, bajulans legem et prophetas ad testimonium assertionis Ecclesiae, ut nos honoremus per sacramentum quod nuntiat illa per litteram.
